title: SourceTerms
description: What each source's own terms say about the use this project makes of it, read once and written down. Two readings are worth the same: a host that permits the uses this project makes, and a host that does not. A host nobody has read is not in this file at all, and silence here is not permission. Recording the permission is what stops the next pass reading the same notice again, and recording the refusal is what stops it publishing the same source again. A refusal is never a judgement about the source: the best route a reader could have had may be one this project cannot carry.

purpose.description: Why this file exists, for whoever finds it without the surrounding context.

sources.description: One entry per host. A host, not a page: terms govern a site, and an organisation this project cannot quote is not quotable one address at a time.

host.description: The host as it appears in an address, without a scheme, a path or a leading www. A subdomain is its own entry: a permission read on one host was not read on another.

uses.description: A notice answers one use at a time, and a single verdict for a host says more than any notice says. A record makes exactly two uses of a source: it quotes words from the page, and it sends the reader to it. Both have to be permitted for a record to stand, so either one refused stops a build. A use nobody read is UNKNOWN, which is not permission.

quote.description: Reproducing words from the page, which every record here rests on.

link.description: Sending a reader to the page. A notice may permit the first and reserve this one, which is why they are asked separately.

extract.description: Taking entries out of a listing the host publishes, which is not the same as quoting one page of it and has its own right attached in the EU. A record never shows this use, so the citation check cannot see it: a directory the research walked and never cited leaves no trace in a published record at all. `npm run measure:discovery` says how many leads each host supplied, which is the number this answer should be read against.

ground.description: TERMS: a published notice was read, and the quote below is what it says. REQUEST_WITHDRAWAL: the operator asked not to appear, which the site's footer promises in six languages to honour. PERMISSION_GRANTED: the operator was asked and said yes, which is the opposite thing and must never be recorded as the same one. Only a reading of a notice carries a quote.

finding.description: What the reading concluded, in plain language, including the conditions a permission carries. Never the name of a person: an operator who asked is an operator, not somebody identified here.

readOn.description: The day the notice was read, or the day the request arrived. A reading has a shelf life and terms change.

termsUrl.description: Where the notice lives, so somebody can read it again rather than trust this file.

quote.description: The sentence the reading rests on, word for word and in its own language. A reading nobody can check is an opinion.

route.description: What would change the outcome, where anything would. Most notices reserve permission rather than refuse it forever, and saying so stops a later pass treating a refusal as permanent.

then.description: A reading of a document names the document and quotes it. Without both, nobody can tell a prohibition from a precaution, and a precaution is how a useful route gets lost.
